Birthday dinner dress code
All black elegance · Sunday 20 Dec

For the birthday dinner, we dress up. Think sleek, tailored and entirely black.

Ladies

Floor-length gowns, satin and sequins. Keep the outfit black.

Gentlemen

A tailored black suit, black shirt and polished black shoes. Look sharp.

Keep the outfit black, but jewellery and accessories can be fun and any colour.

Sunset cruise dress code
White & cream · Saturday 19 Dec
White
Ivory
Cream
Champagne

The look

Flowy dresses or cover-ups, linen and light cotton, in white, ivory and cream. Swimsuits can be any colour.

On the boat

Flat or soft-soled shoes only, as heels and decks do not mix. Bring a light layer, as it gets breezy on the water once the sun starts to drop.

Packing list ▼
So nothing gets left behind

Documents & money

  • PassportValid 30 days past return, 2 blank pages
  • Visa, if you need one
  • Flight details and a copy of your passport
  • Travel insurance
  • Debit and credit card, plus some rand for tips and small buys

Evening looks

  • An all-black outfit for the birthday dinner
  • A white or cream outfit for the cruise
  • Smart casual outfits for the other eveningsNo pressure to dress up, but you may want to look nice
  • Black dress shoes and comfy flat shoes
  • A wrap or light jacket for breezy nights

Daytime clothes

  • Light, breathable outfits for 25–30°C days
  • Two swimsuits and a cover-up
  • A light jacket or windbreakerTable Mountain and the boat are cooler
  • Comfy walking shoes or trainersBo-Kaap's cobbles and the cableway
  • Neutral colours for safari: khaki, olive, sand

Sun & beach

  • Sunscreen SPF 30–50 and lip balm
  • Sunglasses and a hat
  • Beach bag and a quick-dry towel
  • Insect repellent for evenings and safari

Health & toiletries

  • Any prescription meds, in your hand luggage
  • Plasters and blister cream
  • Motion sickness tablets for the boat
  • Pain relief and stomach tablets
  • Makeup
  • Your usual toiletries, hair and skin products

Tech & extras

  • South Africa plug adapterType M, the large 3-pin. UK plugs will not fit
  • Phone charger and a power bank
  • A small cross-body bag, with low-key valuables
  • Reusable water bottle
  • A hand fan
A note on safety ▼
Worth a read before you travel

A few of you have understandably asked about safety in South Africa this year, given the news coverage of xenophobic violence against African nationals, including Nigerians, since the spring. I take that seriously and wanted to be upfront rather than just reassuring you.

That violence has been real, but it's been concentrated in specific areas - Johannesburg, Pretoria and Durban - and aimed at people living and working there, not at short-term visitors. We'll be in Camps Bay, an affluent seafront suburb with its own private security patrols and CCTV coverage, and one of the lowest crime profiles in Cape Town. The villa itself also has on-site security.

I've spoken directly to people who live there, including Nigerians and South Africans, and they've all echoed the same message.

A few sensible precautions: we'll move around as a group, especially after dark, use Uber or booked transport rather than walking late at night, and keep valuables low-key in public. Cape Town's tourist areas - the Waterfront, Camps Bay, the Winelands - are well-patrolled and busy with visitors year-round.

Visa requirements ▼
What you'll need, by passport
BritishNo visa needed
Free 90-day visitor's permit on arrival.
USNo visa needed
Free 90-day visitor's permit on arrival.
NigerianVisa required
Apply via VFS Global (Lagos) or the South African High Commission (Abuja), form BI‑84. Processing takes roughly 10–15 working days – please apply in November to be safe.
ThaiNo visa needed
Visa-free entry, 30-day visitor's permit on arrival.
For everyone: passport valid at least 30 days past your return date, with 2 consecutive blank visa pages. Nigerian applicants will also need proof of funds, an employment/leave letter, and proof of accommodation - message me directly if you need proof of accommodation for your application, and I'll send it over.
